Balakathā:
Is the power of a Tathāgata shared with disciples? Yes.
Is the power of a Tathāgata the power of a disciple, and is the power of a disciple the power of a Tathāgata?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is the power of a Tathāgata shared with disciples?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is that very power of the Tathāgata the power of the disciple, and is that very power of the disciple the power of the Tathāgata?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] … No.
Is the power of a Tathāgata shared with disciples? Yes.
Is the power of a Tathāgata of the same kind as the power of a disciple, and is the power of a disciple of the same kind as the power of a Tathāgata?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the power of a Tathāgata shared with the disciples? Yes.

Is the former application, the former conduct, the proclamation of the Dhamma, and the teaching of the Dhamma of a disciple exactly like the former application, the former conduct, the proclamation of the Dhamma, and the teaching of the Dhamma of a Tathāgata?
One should not say so… [etc.
… Is the power of a Tathāgata shared with disciples?
“Yes.
“Is the Tathāgata the Victor, the Teacher, the Perfectly Enlightened One, the All-Knowing, the All-Seeing, the Lord of Dhamma, and the Refuge of Dhamma?
“Yes.”
Is the Jina, the Teacher, the Fully Enlightened One, the All-Knowing, the All-Seeing, the Lord of Dhamma,
and the Refuge of Dhamma a mere disciple? One should not say so… [and so on]… Is the power of a Tathāgata shared with disciples?
“Yes.

“Then is the Tathāgata the arouser of the unarisen path, the producer of the unproduced path, the declarer of the undeclared path; is he the knower of the path, the discoverer of the path, the one skilled in the path?
“Yes.”

Is a disciple one who causes the unarisen path to arise, brings about the unproduced path, proclaims the unproclaimed path—one who knows the path, understands the path, and is skilled in the path? “Yes,” you say.
“Is a disciple all-knowing and all-seeing?
You must not say so... [and so on].
Does a disciple know what is possible and what is impossible? Yes.
If a disciple knows what is possible and what is impossible, then indeed, it must be said:
“Knowledge of what is possible and what is impossible as it really is is a power of the Tathāgata, not shared with disciples.
Does a disciple know, according to their basis and cause, the ripening of the undertaking of kamma in the past, future, and present? Yes.
If a disciple knows, according to their basis and cause, the ripening of past, future, and present karmic actions, then indeed it must be said:
“The knowledge that truly understands, according to its basis and cause, the ripening of past, future, and present karmic actions is a power of the Tathāgata shared with disciples.
Does a disciple know the path leading everywhere?
“Yes, [he does].
“If a disciple knows the practice that leads everywhere, then indeed, sir, you must say:
‘The Tathāgata’s power consisting in knowledge of the practice that leads everywhere, as it really is, is shared with disciples.’”
Does a disciple know the world as having many elements and diverse elements? Yes.
Since a disciple knows the world as having many elements and diverse elements, surely it must be said:
“Knowledge of the world as it really is—with its many elements and its manifold elements—is a power of the Tathāgata, not shared with disciples.
Does a disciple know the diversity of inclinations among beings?
Yes, he does.
If a disciple knows the diversity of inclinations of beings, then indeed it must be said:
“The knowledge of the diversity of inclinations of beings as they really are is a power of the Tathāgata shared with disciples.
Does a disciple know the defilement, the purification, and the emergence regarding the meditative absorptions, liberations, concentrations, and attainments?

“Yes. “If it is true that a disciple knows the defilement, the purification, and the emergence of the meditative absorptions (jhāna), liberations (vimokkha), concentrations (samādhi), and attainments (samāpatti), then indeed, sir,

you must admit that the Tathāgata’s power consisting in knowledge of the defilement, purification, and emergence of the meditative absorptions, liberations, concentrations, and attainments as they really are, is shared with disciples.”
Does a disciple know the recollection of past lives? Yes.
If a disciple knows the recollection of past lives, then indeed it must be said:
“Recollection of past lives as it really is is a power of the Tathāgata, shared with disciples.
Does a disciple know the passing away and rebirth of beings?
Yes, he does.
If a disciple knows the passing away and rebirth of beings, then indeed it should be said:
"The knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings as they really are is a power of the Tathāgata shared with disciples.
Is it not the case that the taints are exhausted for the Tathāgata and the taints are also exhausted for the disciple?
“Yes.
“Is there any distinction between the Tathāgata and his disciple as regards the destruction of the taints or the liberation through the destruction of the taints?
“There is none.”

If there is no difference whatsoever between the destruction of the taints of a Tathāgata and the destruction of the taints of a disciple, or between the liberation of a Tathāgata and the liberation of a disciple, then indeed, sir, you must say:
"The knowledge of things as they really are regarding the destruction of the taints is a power of a Tathāgata shared with disciples.
Is it the case that the knowledge of things as they really are regarding the destruction of the taints is a power of a Tathāgata shared with disciples?
“Yes.
“Then, is the knowledge of things as they truly are regarding what is possible and what is impossible a power of the Tathāgata shared with his disciples?
“One should not say so…” [and so on].
Is the Tathāgata’s power consisting in knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it really is shared with disciples?
Yes. Is the Tathāgata’s power consisting in knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings as they really is shared with disciples? Yes.
It should not be said thus… [as before] …Is the knowledge of things as they truly are regarding what is possible and impossible a power of the Tathāgata that is not shared with disciples? Yes.
Is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it really is a power of the Tathāgata not shared with disciples?
One should not say so… [and so on] … Is the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings as they really is a power of the Tathāgata not shared with disciples?
“Yes.
“Then, is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it really is a power of the Tathāgata that is not shared with disciples?
“One must not say so…” [and so on].
Is the Tathāgata’s power consisting in knowledge of the degrees of the faculties as they really are a power not shared by disciples?
Yes. Is the Tathāgata’s power consisting in knowledge of what is possible and impossible as it really are a power not shared by disciples? Yes.
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is the knowledge of the higher and lower faculties of others as they really are a power of the Tathāgata that is not shared with his disciples?
Yes. … [as before] …
Is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it really is a power of the Tathāgata not shared with disciples?
One should not say so… [etc.
… Is the knowledge of what is possible and impossible as it really is a power of the Tathāgata shared with disciples?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Is the Tathāgata’s power consisting in knowledge of the higher and lower faculties of others as they really are shared with the disciples?
“One should not say so,” etc. …pe…
Is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it really is a power of the Tathāgata shared with disciples?
Yes. Is the knowledge of the higher and lower faculties of others as they really are a power of the Tathāgata shared with disciples? Yes.
It should not be stated thus … [as before] … The Discussion on Power is finished.
